blocks.text: You've had on → oli since Lesson 2, but that's an irregular verb. Most Finnish verbs build their past tense the same predictable way — and reviewers use it constantly to narrate their own experience: sain (I got), vein (I took), soitin (I called), kuulin (I heard). Today you get the pattern behind all of them.

blocks.title: First person vs. the passive
blocks.text: Lesson 4 gave you the passive (tehtiin, vaihdettiin) for describing what the shop did. This lesson gives you the mirror image: what the reviewer personally did or experienced. Notice how reviews switch between the two — sain palvelua (I got service, personal) next to autoon tehtiin huolto (a service was done, impersonal). Both are needed to tell the full story.

blocks.content: Most Finnish verbs build the past tense the same way: stem + {-i-|grammar|past tense marker|-ed} + personal ending. Soittaa (to call) → soit + i + n → {soitin|grammar|1st person past|I called}. Kuulla (to hear) → kuul + i + n → {kuulin|grammar|1st person past|I heard}. Käyttää (to use) → käyt + i + n → {käytin|grammar|1st person past|I used}. Same -n for 'I' you already know from suosittelen.

items.en: I heard about the place from a friend.

items.fi: {Käytin|grammar|1st person past|I used} tätä autohuoltoa monta vuotta.
items.en: I used this car service centre for many years.

blocks.text: Piece 2 — Frequent irregulars: sain, vein, näin

blocks.title: Same job, shorter shape
blocks.text: A handful of very common verbs fuse the -i- straight into the stem instead of adding it separately, so the result looks shorter: saada (to get) → {sain|grammar|1st person past, irregular|I got}, viedä (to take/bring) → {vein|grammar|1st person past, irregular|I took}, nähdä (to see) → {näin|grammar|1st person past, irregular|I saw}. These appear so often in reviews that it's worth just learning the whole words directly rather than deriving them each time.

items.fi: {Sain|grammar|1st person past, irregular|I got} ajan nopeasti.
{Vein|grammar|1st person past, irregular|I took} autoni korjaamoon.
items.en: I took my car to the repair shop.

items.fi: {Näin|grammar|1st person past, irregular|I saw} hinta-arvion etukäteen.
items.en: I saw the price estimate in advance.

blocks.content: For 'he/she/it', the past tense uses the exact same stem + -i-, but with no personal ending at all. Soitin (I called) becomes {soitti|grammar|3rd person past|he/she called} — just drop the -n. This is the form you'll see most often in reviews describing what the shop or a staff member did: korjaamo lupasi soittaa, 'the shop promised to call'.

items.en: The repair shop called the next day.

items.fi: Hän {lupasi|grammar|3rd person past|promised} korjata virheen ilmaiseksi.
items.en: They promised to fix the mistake for free.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: How did you get an appointment at the repair shop?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Soitin heille, ja sain ajan nopeasti.
lines.en: I called them, and I got an appointment quickly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Vein sen sinne, ja korjaamo soitti heti, kun se oli valmis.
lines.en: I took it there, and the repair shop called right away when it was ready.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: You now have two past tense engines running side by side: on → oli (Lesson 2, one irregular verb) and stem + -i- + ending (this lesson, almost every other verb). When you meet a brand new verb in the past tense, first check: does it look like oli's family, or does it have that telltale -i- sitting in the middle? That single question will tell you which pattern you're looking at.

blocks.content: Sain: SAIN (one syllable, the 'ai' glides like English 'eye'). Soitin: SOI-tin (two syllables, 'oi' like 'oy' in 'boy'). Soitti: SOIT-ti (the double 't' is held — soitin and soitti sound close, listen for that final n vs i).

rows.en: he/she promised (3rd person past of luvata)

blocks.title: What you now own
items: the regular past tense pattern: stem + -i- + personal ending
sain, vein, näin — three frequent irregular past-tense verbs, learned as whole words
soitti, lupasi — the he/she past tense, same stem but no personal ending
you can now narrate your own experience in the past, not just describe states with oli
you can tell irregular verbs like oli apart from the regular -i- pattern on sight
